newsitem.title: INDIA: WTO says India steps must be matched by partners.
newsitem.headline: WTO says India steps must be matched by partners.

text.p: India's steps in opening its markets and dismantling trade barriers must be matched by her trading partners, World Trade Organisation (WTO) Deputy Director General Chulsu Kim said on Friday.
"Globalisation implies that India's efforts receive a matching response from her trading partners," Kim told an international conference on Asian markets in the Indian capital.
"An open trading environment will be needed to support India's desire to compete on equal terms with her trading partners for opportunities in the world marketplace."
Kim said despite India's reforms process, launched in 1991, the country remains in many respects "one of the most protected markets in Asia".

He noted that tariffs remain considerably higher than in East Asian countries, and quantitative restrictions still apply to 30 percent of items imported into India, particularly consumer goods. Foreign direct investment was restricted in some sectors.

"If India is to attain the growth pattern of seven percent and to receive $10 billion in foreign direct investment...it appears that renewed impetus needs to be given to the reform programme," Kim said.

"The acceleration of reform would be necessary to overcome the recent slowdown of exports and industrial production, and overcome the serious infrastructure bottleneck faced by Indian companies," Kim told the conference.

India's exports rose to $27.07 billion between April 1996 and January 1997 from $25.49 billion a year earlier, but the trade deficit for the same 1996/97 period rose to $4.29 billion from $4.06 in the corresponding 1995/96 period.
Industrial production growth slowed to 9.8 percent during April-October 1996 from 11.7 percent a year earlier.
Kim recommended an elimination of quantitative restrictions on consumer goods imports and a further liberalisation of the foreign investment regime.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram, who unveiled a market-friendly budget a week ago, said in a newspaper interview published on Friday that liberalisation of consumer goods imports would help boost India's "sluggish" import growth and increase customs revenue.
"It is viable and necessary to open up consumer goods imports. Opening up of imports is good in itself. It is an advance on trade policy," he said.
